key_insight: Halide species in mixed Cs/Rb lead-halide perovskites do not mix randomly; they order into layered arrangements that can shift structural phase-transition temperatures by up to 100 K and reshape the phase diagram.
engineering_relevance: Controlling halide and A-site composition is a practical lever for tuning stability and phase behavior in perovskite solar-cell materials, especially near device-relevant temperatures.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for CsxRb1-xPbBr3yI3-3y, CsxRb1-xPbBr3yCl3-3y, and CsxRb1-xPbCl3yI3-3y.
Ran large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample both configurational disorder and vibrational effects.
Mapped miscibility gaps and halide ordering across compositions and temperatures to connect them with structural phase transitions.
evidence_signal: The simulations show miscibility gaps in all three binary halide systems, with Br–Cl and Br–I gaps closing at low temperature, Cl–I persisting above room temperature, and ordering emerging from 200 K to 500 K.
watch_item: MLIP predictions depend on the quality and coverage of the underlying DFT training data, so extrapolation to untrained compositions or defect-rich real materials should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
